questions.q: What happens to existing Account records when a pipeline deploys a new required field to production?
options: The field is automatically populated on every existing record
All existing records are deleted
Nothing -- a metadata deploy doesn't touch existing records at all; populating the field is a separate, deliberate data operation
The deployment fails automatically until the field is populated
questions.explain: Metadata deploys move structural definitions, not records -- a new field appearing on an object doesn't by itself change any existing row's data.

questions.q: Why are Custom Metadata Type records treated differently from ordinary custom object records in a deployment?
options: They aren't treated differently at all
Custom Metadata Type records can only be created manually through Setup, never via CLI
They require a separate Salesforce license to use
A Custom Metadata Type's records are themselves metadata, so they can be included in a deployment manifest and deploy automatically along with everything else
questions.explain: Custom Metadata Type records are metadata, not ordinary data rows -- which is exactly why they're the standard place to put configuration values that need to travel automatically between environments via a deploy.

questions.q: What does sf data export tree produce when exporting Accounts together with their related Contacts?
options: A flat CSV file with no relationship information
A compiled binary of the records
Nested JSON in sObject tree format that preserves the parent-child relationship between the records
A PDF report
questions.explain: The tree export/import commands work with a nested JSON sObject tree format specifically so parent-child relationships (like an Account's related Contacts) survive the round trip.

questions.q: Per the official docs, roughly what volume of records are sf data export tree / import tree intended for?
options: Millions of records, replacing the Bulk API entirely
Exactly one record at a time
There is no volume limit of any kind
Small, relationship-aware datasets -- the export query is capped at a maximum of 2,000 records, with the Bulk API recommended for larger volumes
questions.explain: The tree commands are meant for small reference datasets (export capped at 2,000 records per query); genuinely large data movement should go through the Bulk API path instead.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a seed-data import for a scratch org typically has to run after the metadata deploy, not before or during it?
options: Because you can't import a record into an org that doesn't yet have the object/fields that record's data depends on
Because sf data import tree cannot run in the same pipeline as a metadata deploy
Because data imports always take longer than metadata deploys
There is no ordering dependency between the two
questions.explain: A data import depends on the target object and fields already existing in the org -- so the metadata deploy that creates them has to complete first.
